correctness.rationale: Explicit stable-focus Jacobian and matrix exponential yield the frozen-input prey response; |sin(qt)|<=qt gives a uniform 2/e bound. The exact L1 predator response is kappa*coth(pi*alpha/(4q)). Variation of constants and an exponential-semigroup bootstrap provide O(epsilon^2) errors uniformly for all t>=0 and bounded inputs. A resonant sine at omega=sqrt(d) has prey gain c/alpha, forcing a finite prey crossing with predator strictly above threshold. At a possible grazing contact an f1 Filippov continuation exists until inward entry; the two prey-below-threshold fields have negative N derivative, and predator later decays. A constant frozen input remains entirely in the coexistence compartment and approaches its positive equilibrium. An executed extracted verifier checks 79 matrix identities, 39 frozen profiles and three transversal sinusoidal events; finite checks do not certify the theorem.

value.rationale: A natural counterfactual in frequency-induced tipping is whether every fixed environmental condition in a driving interval can be safe from the same initial population state while a periodic schedule causes extinction. This theorem supplies such a nontrivial mechanism at arbitrarily weak amplitude in every stable-focus parameter family, with explicit admissible thresholds, a universal sharp 2/e step-versus-sine gain separation, and an exact predator barrier bound; it goes beyond merely reproducing a harmonic peak or numerically detecting tipping.
